title: Grade 5 Science — Thu, Jun 19
description: Respiratory System — Day 4 of 5: Gas exchange in alveoli
subject: science

questions.question: Gas exchange is the process of:
options: Moving air in and out of lungs
Oxygen passing from alveoli into the blood and CO₂ passing from blood into alveoli
questions.explanation: Gas exchange occurs at the alveoli: O₂ from inhaled air crosses the thin alveolar walls into blood capillaries; CO₂ from blood crosses into the alveoli to be exhaled.

questions.question: Gas exchange occurs by the process of:
options: Diffusion (movement from high concentration to low concentration)
questions.explanation: Diffusion: O₂ is at HIGH concentration in inhaled air → moves to LOW concentration in blood. CO₂ is at HIGH concentration in blood → moves to LOW in alveoli.

questions.question: For efficient gas exchange, alveoli must be:
options: Thick-walled and far from blood vessels
Thin-walled, moist, and surrounded by many capillaries
questions.explanation: Alveoli have: thin walls (short diffusion distance), moist surfaces (gases dissolve first), rich blood supply (capillaries). All three maximise gas exchange.

questions.question: After gas exchange, blood leaving the lungs is:
questions.explanation: After gas exchange, blood carries lots of oxygen (oxygenated blood). It flows via pulmonary veins → left heart → pumped to body cells.

questions.question: Blood arriving at the lungs (from the body) is:
options: Rich in CO₂ and low in O₂ (deoxygenated)
questions.explanation: Blood returning from body cells has given up its oxygen and picked up CO₂. It arrives at the lungs as deoxygenated blood, to be re-oxygenated.

questions.question: Haemoglobin is:
options: A type of white blood cell
A protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin is the red protein in red blood cells. It binds to O₂ (forming oxyhaemoglobin) in the lungs and releases O₂ at body cells.

questions.question: Why does blood look red?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin contains iron (Fe). When iron binds with oxygen, it forms bright red oxyhaemoglobin. Deoxygenated haemoglobin is darker red (appears blue in veins through skin).

questions.question: Carbon monoxide (CO, from vehicle exhaust) is dangerous because:
options: It binds to haemoglobin MORE strongly than oxygen, blocking O₂ transport
questions.explanation: CO binds to haemoglobin about 200× more strongly than O₂. This blocks haemoglobin from carrying oxygen, causing cells to suffocate even with normal breathing.

questions.question: What does the body do with the CO₂ collected from cells?
options: Sends it to the lungs via blood; exhaled out
questions.explanation: CO₂ is carried by blood (partly dissolved in plasma, partly as bicarbonate) to the lungs, where it crosses into alveoli and is exhaled out.

questions.question: The pulmonary circuit refers to:
options: Blood flow from heart to body cells
Blood flow between heart and lungs (for gas exchange)
questions.explanation: Pulmonary circuit: right heart → pulmonary arteries → lungs (gas exchange) → pulmonary veins → left heart. This is the 'heart-to-lungs' circuit.

questions.question: High altitude (e.g. mountains at 4,000 m) has less oxygen per breath. What happens to breathing rate?
options: It increases — body tries to get more oxygen
questions.explanation: At altitude, air pressure is lower — less O₂ per breath. The body compensates by increasing breathing rate and eventually producing more red blood cells.

questions.question: Surfactant is a substance in alveoli that:
options: Prevents alveoli from collapsing by reducing surface tension in the moist walls
questions.explanation: Surfactant reduces surface tension in alveoli, preventing them from collapsing after each exhalation. Premature babies often lack surfactant — a medical emergency.

questions.question: Plants and animals are linked by gas exchange. Plants produce ___ during photosynthesis, which animals breathe in.
questions.explanation: Plants produce oxygen during photosynthesis and absorb CO₂. Animals breathe in O₂ and exhale CO₂. They are in a gas exchange cycle with each other.

questions.question: Why is smoking harmful to the respiratory system?
options: Tar damages alveoli, cilia, and airways; nicotine causes addiction; CO blocks haemoglobin
Smoking only affects the heart, not the lungs
questions.explanation: Cigarette smoke: Tar destroys alveoli (emphysema), paralyses cilia (mucus accumulates), causes lung cancer. CO blocks O₂ transport. Nicotine constricts airways.

questions.question: Summary: In the alveoli, ___ moves from air into blood, and ___ moves from blood into air:
questions.explanation: O₂ diffuses from alveolar air (high O₂) → blood capillaries (low O₂). CO₂ diffuses from blood (high CO₂) → alveolar air (low CO₂). Then exhaled out.
